rationale: No race telemetry exists yet (iteration 0), so this is a conservative baseline rather than a tuned design. Geometry: five sensors spread across 0.08 m (x = -0.04 to 0.04) at y = 0.05 m ahead of the axle, so the array covers the 25 mm tape with overlap and gives a usable signal on moderate bends. Sensor size 0.012 m is a compromise between resolution and tape coverage. The wheel track, radius, mass and body dimensions are mid-range values that give a stable yaw inertia. Controller: base_speed 1.6 (PWM about 80 percent) is high enough to approach the 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s while leaving headroom for turns. Weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1] make the signal scale about one unit per sensor offset, so kp = 5 gives a moderate steering response (about 1750 PWM counts per unit of signal). A small kd = 0.3 damps oscillation and a small ki = 0.05 removes bias from the motor mismatch. line_loss is 'last_direction' so the robot keeps turning the way it was heading when it drifts off the tape. Expected result: the robot completes the oval and s-bend with modest error, and the first race's telemetry (rms_error, oscillation, line-loss count) will show whether the speed is too high or the gain too low or too high.
